narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while the rest had six or more years. This shorter track record made the system less confident in your long-term commitment.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. This strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving, as having external opportunities often signals that someone is considering or likely to move on.

Third, the fact that you reported no psychological exhaustion worked in your favor and pulled the prediction slightly back toward staying. Most employees the model sees as stayers also report low mental fatigue, so this was a positive element in your profile.

Taken together, your limited experience and the presence of outside opportunities outweighed the protective effect of good mental wellbeing, leading to the 70% likelihood of departure. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether additional responsibilities or clearer advancement paths could increase your sense of stability. You may also want to reflect on how those external offers align with your longer-term plans. (248 words)
